name: LSerial
author: Niklas Sjöberg

provenance.note: Unregistered shareware build; the binary emits 'UNREGISTERED SHAREWARE version of LSerial!' banners. Attributed to Niklas Sjoberg, the LDos author — inferred here from the shared naming and demo layout, and since confirmed by the Ultimate Amiga AMOS Factory archive listing.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified. The AMOS PD Library on CD (Weird Science, 1994), archive.org item cdrom-amospdcd. The disc's own Documents/Copyrights states Weird Science claims no copyright over the material, that parts are shareware with fees due, and that users should make no assumption that anything on it is public domain. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: Niklas Sjoberg's serial.device wrapper, written because AMOS's own would not survive a close and reopen: "AMOS's serial didn't work in 1.0/1.1, in 1.2/1.3 it worked, but only sometimes and only a little :-)". Twelve keywords are a thin, honest layer over exec's DoIO/SendIO/CheckIO on three IOExtSer requests; the other three are Linkey$, Lser Status and Lxpr. Read from the 10,532-byte hunk (19 jump-table entries, 15 keywords) against LserialV21.DOC, which gives every argument order, the whole io_Status bit table and the entire XPR contract, and the two agree everywhere. The slot is the doc's, unusually firmly: "you MUST place LSerial as extension number eleven (11) ... If you MUST or NEED to have it configured as another number then send me a disk full of nice programs", and routine 0's $198(a5) agrees. `Lxpr` is APPROXIMATED: 7,220 bytes and a whole XPR host in one keyword -- the doc explains why it is one keyword, "the AMOS compiler treats all functions as local, as it datas" -- whose dispatch, NUL-termination checks and library-absent arms are all exact, but whose transfers need an xpr*.library that is not modelled. Two defects: `Lser Get`'s size guard is unsigned, so zero is refused and a negative count passes as four billion; and `Linkey$`'s `cmp.b #$5a,d1 / bcc` skips the lowercase fold for 'Z' itself, so CONTROL with a shifted Z gives Chr$(250) where every other shifted letter gives 1 to 25. One DEVIATION beyond Lxpr: this is the UNREGISTERED build -- its $VER cookie says LSerial_V21_UnRegistered -- and every one of the ten error paths flashes COLOR00 and BPLCON1 white, flips to the Workbench screen, prints " UNREGISTERED SHAREWARE version of LSerial!  Author really should register!" and flips back before raising. The error is reproduced; the nag is not.
